data.name: Haidar
data.gender_notes: Haidar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Haidarah' which means 'lion'. In Islamic tradition, Haidar is a name given to the prophet Solomon and is associated with strength, courage, and royalty. The name Haidar carries the meaning “The Lion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Haidar usually hope their child will grow to embody the lion and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.name: Haidar
in_english.long_meaning: Haidar is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, meaning brave, powerful, strong, or lion-like. It is derived from the Arabic root 'h-d-r' which connotes the idea of being strong, courageous, and powerful. In Islamic tradition, Haidar is often used as an epithet for Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, the cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad, who was renowned for his bravery and strength in battle. The name Haidar is popular across various Muslim cultures and is often bestowed upon boys born into families who value courage, resilience, and leadership qualities.
